title: Frontend: close coverage to 90% gate, verify Storybook + no-network invariants
description: Closing pass once every frontend-* feature task has landed: run the real coverage gate across the whole app, close any gaps, and verify the cross-cutting invariants (no live network calls, Storybook builds clean) hold for the app as a whole, not just per-task. Mirrors the backend's check-coverage/test-90 skill pair, applied here as one task since there's no dedicated frontend skill yet.

checklist.step: Run `npm run test:coverage` (vitest --coverage) against the full app; identify every file below the 90% lines/branches/functions/statements threshold from docs/architecture/Testing.md.

Write the missing tests to close each gap — prefer testing real behavior (an interaction, a rendered error state) over trivial assertions that only exist to move a number, per Testing.md's 'What 90% Coverage Does Not Guarantee' section.
Grep the whole frontend/ test suite for any accidental real network call (a bare fetch()/axios call not going through MSW, or a test missing its MSW handler) — fix any found.

Confirm `npm run build-storybook` still succeeds and every components/common/ component has both a test and a story (re-verify frontend-common-components' bar holds after all feature work landed, since a later task could have quietly skipped it).
Confirm `npm run build` (production build) succeeds with no TypeScript errors.

decisions.decision: Closed StockDetailPage.tsx's branch-coverage gap (88.88% → 100%) by adding a test that renders it under a route with no `:ticker` param, asserting the `ticker || 'Stock Detail'` header fallback and that useStockAnalysis's `enabled: ticker.length > 0` guard skips the query (no loading/error UI renders). Left two other pre-existing sub-90%-file lines uncovered on purpose rather than fake-covering them: PositionsTable.tsx:87 (`if (!pendingDelete) return` in handleConfirmDelete) and PriceChart.tsx:112 (`if (finiteBars.length === 0) return` in the chart-creation effect) are both TypeScript-narrowing guards that are provably unreachable through any real user interaction — MUI's Dialog unmounts its Confirm button while closed (so handleConfirmDelete can only ever fire with pendingDelete already set), and PriceChart's own `hasBars` (identical filter) gates whether the chart container even renders, so the effect's `!container` branch always fires first when there are zero finite bars. Writing a test to hit either would mean fabricating an app state that can't occur, which Testing.md's 'What 90% Coverage Does Not Guarantee' and this skill's step 4 both flag as not meeting the bar in spirit. Both files (94.44%/92.85% and 97.43%/95.83% resp.) and the suite overall (99.43%/99.21%/100%/99.41%) already clear every dimension of the 90% gate by a wide margin, so no coverage shortfall remains that these two lines would need to close.
decisions.rationale: Alternative considered and rejected: deleting the two guards to eliminate the branches entirely. Rejected because they're not dead code in the sense of no code path ever reaching the surrounding function — they're required for TypeScript's null-narrowing given `useParams`/local nullable state typing, and removing them would trade a harmless always-false guard for a runtime crash risk if the surrounding component's rendering logic is ever refactored in a way that breaks the current invariant. Keeping the defensive guard (undocumented previously) plus this decision entry is safer than deleting real safety code just to chase a per-file number the gate doesn't actually require.

review.notes:
Full review of PR #71 (branch task/frontend-test-90). Diff is small and well-scoped: one new test (StockDetailPage.test.tsx, no-ticker-param fallback/disabled-query branch) plus task-board bookkeeping; no application source changed beyond the test.

Verification performed:
- `npm run test:coverage` (vitest --coverage): 32 files / 168 tests pass. Overall 99.43%/99.21%/100%/99.41% (stmts/branch/funcs/lines) — clears the 90% gate by a wide margin on all four dimensions, both overall and per-file (worst files: PositionsTable.tsx 94.44%/92.85%, PriceChart.tsx 97.43%/95.83%, both still >90% on every dimension).
- `npm run lint`: clean. `npm run build` (tsc -b && vite build): clean, no TS errors. `npm run build-storybook`: succeeds.
- Verified every `src/components/common/*` component (ConfidenceGauge, ConfirmDialog, DataTable, EmptyState, ErrorState, LoadingState, PageHeader, PercentChange, SignalBadge, StatCard) has both a `.test.tsx` and a `.stories.tsx` — bar holds app-wide, not just for this PR's own components (none added here).
- Verified the no-live-network safety net isn't just asserted but actually works: `tests/setup.ts` calls `server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' })`, wired via `vite.config.ts`'s `setupFiles`. Empirically confirmed by adding a scratch test that called `fetch('http://example.invalid/...')` with no MSW handler — it failed the suite with MSW's 'intercepted a request without a matching request handler' error, exactly as intended; removed the scratch file afterward (git status clean). Confirmed `api/client.ts` is the only non-test `fetch()` call site in the whole frontend.
- Independently traced (did not just trust the decisions entry) both claimed-unreachable lines: PositionsTable.tsx:87 (`if (!pendingDelete) return` in handleConfirmDelete) — the Confirm button only exists in the DOM while ConfirmDialog is open (MUI Dialog unmounts its content when closed, no `keepMounted`), and `open` is exactly `pendingDelete !== null`, so the handler can only ever fire with `pendingDelete` already set. PriceChart.tsx:112 (`if (finiteBars.length === 0) return` in the chart-creation effect) — the chart container (`containerRef`) only renders when `hasBars` is true in the same render pass that computed `historyQuery.data`, and the effect (keyed only on `historyQuery.data`) recomputes `finiteBars` from that identical data/filter, so `container` truthy and `finiteBars.length === 0` can't co-occur. Both genuinely unreachable through any real user interaction, not a convenience excuse to skip real gaps.
- Ran the `code-review` skill (medium effort) against the PR diff: no correctness, reuse, or simplification findings; it independently reached the same unreachability conclusions above.
- Re-ran the full backend suite for regression due diligence (untouched by this PR): 478 passed, 99.84% coverage, no drop.
- No API/schema changes in this PR, so no openapi.json staleness check applies. No new component/module/dependency/layer added, so architecture-review and the frontend component-placement check (step 7a) don't apply beyond the common/ test+story re-verification above (already done). Task's `decisions` entry (documenting the two left-uncovered lines) is present and substantive, satisfying the decision-memory requirement — no checklist item here is phrased as an undecided 'decide X'.
- This PR's diff makes no application-code change a user would click through (only a test file), so the browser-walkthrough step (9) doesn't apply here — stated explicitly rather than silently skipped. The underlying pages (StockDetailPage, PriceChart, PositionsTable) already received real browser walkthroughs on their own feature PRs (#68/#69 etc.).

No blocking findings. No non-blocking findings either — nothing to file as a follow-up task for this review pass.
